headline: Record revenue and membership growth drive a raised outlook
summary_short: Net revenue reached $1.22 billion (+43% y/y) with GAAP net income of $156.6 million and diluted EPS of $0.12; members grew 35% y/y to 15.8 million as loan originations hit a record $14.8 billion.
summary_long: SoFi delivered its strongest quarter yet: net revenue rose 43% y/y to $1.22 billion, led by net interest income (+52%) from higher average interest-earning assets and cheaper funding, plus fee revenue from the Loan Platform Business, interchange, and brokerage. Adjusted EBITDA grew 44% to $357.8 million (30% margin), a 19th straight quarter above the 'Rule of 40.' Net income was $156.6 million ($0.12 diluted EPS). Members (15.8M) and products (24.4M) hit records, with cross-buy at 51%. Technology Platform revenue fell 23% y/y on a prior client's platform exit. Equity rose to $11.1 billion; cash fell to $3.13 billion as originations hit a record $14.8 billion. Management raised FY2026 adjusted net revenue guidance to $4.75-4.85 billion.

drivers.explanation: Record revenue, member, and product growth; management calls Q2 a 'clear inflection point' driven by durable multi-segment demand and cross-buy into SoFi Plus/Coach.
Net interest income +52% y/y from 49% growth in average interest-earning assets and a 36bp lower cost of funds, plus fee revenue from Loan Platform Business, interchange, and brokerage.
NIM rose 4bps q/q as the average deposit rate ran 156bps below warehouse-facility funding, reflecting continued remixing of the funding base toward deposits.
Cross-buy accelerated to 51% of new products from existing members, up from 43% last quarter, driven by SoFi Plus relaunch and SoFi Coach engagement.
Revenue growth (+43% y/y) outpaced total expense growth (+37% y/y), widening net income margin from 11% to 13%.
Not explained in the release beyond ordinary balance-sheet deployment into loan originations and investment securities during the quarter.
